Conflict: In-Service Agent recommends high-impact thick-walled virgin polymers for durability; Circularity Agent rejects this, recommending a monomaterial polymer to maximize recycling quality.
Decision: Recycled-content monomaterial polypropylene (rPP) with structural ribbing
Rationale: Balances durability requirements under ESPR Annex I (a) with recycled content under (h) and lightweight design under (t) by using structural ribbing to compensate for rPP's lower tensile strength.

Conflict: In-Service Agent recommends threaded fasteners with metal inserts to ensure robust repairability; Circularity Agent rejects this because molded-in metal inserts contaminate the plastic recycling stream, hindering high-purity material recovery.
Decision: Reversible mechanical fasteners (standardized screws and snap-fits) without molded-in metal inserts
Rationale: Satisfies the ease of repair and maintenance under ESPR Annex I (b) while ensuring high-quality recycling and material recovery under (d) and (e) by avoiding inseparable metal-to-plastic joints.

Conflict: Manufacture Agent recommends a synchronous reluctance motor to avoid the toxic emissions and energy-intensive extraction of rare-earth magnets; In-Service Agent recommends a high-efficiency brushless DC (BLDC) motor to maximize use-phase energy efficiency.
Decision: High-efficiency brushless DC (BLDC) motor designed with easily removable/separable rare-earth magnets and recycled copper windings
Rationale: Prioritizes use-phase energy efficiency under ESPR Annex I (g) as a major environmental footprint driver, while satisfying circularity under (d) by ensuring the magnets can be easily extracted before shredding.

Conflict: Manufacture Agent recommends an active cooling fan integrated into the motor shaft to minimize manufacturing waste and material use; In-Service Agent recommends oversized passive heat sinks with dedicated ventilation ducts to eliminate moving parts and maximize reliability.
Decision: Passive cooling via optimized airflow channels using the vacuum's existing working airflow, combined with removable/washable filters and lightweight aluminum fins
Rationale: Satisfies lightweight design under ESPR Annex I (t) by integrating functions (using working airflow for cooling) while avoiding the reliability risks of an active fan, thereby supporting durability under (a).

Conflict: Manufacture Agent recommends a highly integrated monolithic design to simplify assembly and reduce production waste; Circularity Agent recommends a highly modular architecture with toolless component swap to facilitate repair, upgrading, and recycling.
Decision: Semi-modular architecture with standardized fasteners for key functional blocks (motor, cord, filters)
Rationale: Balances ease of repair and maintenance under ESPR Annex I (b) with weight, volume, and material footprint constraints under (j) and (o) by avoiding the excessive material overhead of fully toolless modular connectors.

Conflict: In-Service Agent recommends an automatic cord reel for user convenience and cable protection; Circularity Agent rejects this because the complex reel mechanism contains mixed materials (steel spring, copper contacts, plastic spool) that are difficult to disassemble and recycle.
Decision: Corded mains power connection with a manual, integrated cord-wrap structure on the housing instead of an automatic mechanical cord reel
Rationale: Eliminates hazardous battery waste under ESPR Annex I (r) and avoids the complex, unrecyclable mechanical reel mechanism to satisfy design for recycling under (d), while still providing cable management to protect the cord and maintain durability under (a).
